title: Optimal space–query tradeoff for approximate Voronoi diagrams
formal: For each fixed dimension \(d\ge2\), determine the worst-case minimum storage \(S_d(n,t,\varepsilon)\) of the box-based approximate Voronoi diagrams defined below, for \(n\ge2\), \(1\le t\le n\), and \(0<\varepsilon\le1/2\). Seek matching upper and lower bounds up to powers of \(\log(n/\varepsilon+2)\), uniformly over the full parameter domain.
definitions:
Normalize the n distinct sites to lie in the closed ball of radius epsilon/22 centered at (1/2,…,1/2) inside U=[0,1]^d. A dyadic quadtree box is U or a cube obtained by repeatedly bisecting all coordinate directions. A cell is a quadtree box with at most one strictly smaller contained quadtree box removed; a box with nothing removed is allowed. A diagram is a finite partition of U by such cells, represented by their outer and optional inner boxes. Fix boundary ownership consistently using half-open intervals, with the outer boundary of U included in its adjacent cells.

Each cell C stores a nonempty subset R_C of at most t input sites, and must satisfy \(\min_{r\in R_C}\|q-r\|_2\le(1+\varepsilon)\min_{s\in S}\|q-s\|_2\) for every q assigned to C. This must also hold at input sites, where the right side is zero. Queries outside U use a fixed site: under the chosen normalization its distance is within the required factor. Storage is \(n+\sum_C(1+|R_C|)\), counting sites, cells and representative references; a real coordinate costs one storage unit, independent of bit precision. Shared coordinate storage does not make repeated representative references free.

For each normalized S take the minimum storage over admissible diagrams; S_d is the supremum of those minima over S. The selected target is this geometric storage complexity, not the complexity of arbitrary nearest-neighbor structures. No construction-time bound is imposed. The representation is an editorial explicit box-partition variant of the source’s quadtree setting; a more restrictive balanced hierarchy is not silently required. The requested uniform precision means bounds L and U with L≤S_d≤U and U/L≤C_d log^{a_d}(n/epsilon+2), for constants depending only on d.
answer_criterion: Provide explicit parameter bounds and complete Lean-checked universal upper and worst-case lower proofs with the stated polylogarithmic gap. Upper bounds must count all representatives, and lower bounds must apply to the allowed box partitions. A tradeoff for an unrestricted nearest-neighbor data structure does not by itself determine this storage function.
context:
Arya, Malamatos and Mount analyze diagrams with several representatives in a box-based cell. Their extreme tradeoffs are nearly tight, while their conclusion identifies a gap between the extremes.

Later polytope-membership techniques improve general approximate nearest-neighbor structures. Such results require a separate representation check before being treated as a resolution of a box-diagram question.
why: The tradeoff quantifies the geometric storage needed to reduce approximate nearest-neighbor queries to a small candidate set.

import_provenance.original_title: Optimal space–query tradeoff for approximate Voronoi diagrams
import_provenance.original_statement: For n sites in fixed-dimensional Euclidean space, determine the optimal worst-case size of a (t,ε)-approximate Voronoi diagram: a subdivision into quadtree boxes or differences of boxes, each storing at most t sites, one of which is a (1+ε)-nearest neighbour for every query in that cell. The issue is the full tradeoff between storage and t, rather than a bound at just one endpoint.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: Model qualification: this asks about the geometric size of the restricted representative-based AVD, not the best unrestricted nearest-neighbour data structure. Arya, da Fonseca and Mount’s 2017 polytope-membership methods already improve unrestricted approximate nearest-neighbour space bounds. https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.01696

sentences: An approximate Voronoi diagram partitions a bounded region into simple dyadic cells.
Each cell retains at most t candidate sites that cover all its nearest-neighbor queries approximately.
The target measures total cell and representative storage in the worst case.
Known extreme tradeoffs do not automatically settle every intermediate parameter choice.
The editorial formulation fixes normalization, boundary ownership, storage accounting and polylogarithmic precision.
